scope: Independent static review of the frozen exact-stop command source and its root binding only. No remote action, tests, imports, payload reads, or execution were performed by this reviewer.

excluded_failed_verifier.treatment: Excluded permanently; not queried or targeted.

findings.evidence: The script validates the embedded acceptance bytes against the pinned SHA-256, accepted schema/status, exact native and successful-verifier unit/invocation identities, strict integer exit/update/epoch fields, and 44,760 successful updates. It bounds and O_NOFOLLOW-opens the verifier unit.log, checks stable inode/stat metadata and content SHA before/after reading, derives the pinned result bytes from the accepted offset, and requires the decoded result to be PASS for the exact native unit/invocation. It also prehashes the checker source and provenance metadata against the accepted pins.

Before the stop call, both named units must be loaded, successful, and match the exact invocation IDs with ActiveState=active, SubState=exited, MainPID=0, ExecMainCode=1, and ExecMainStatus=0. The campaign slice must have a non-root control group and no populated cgroup.procs file anywhere in the enumerated descendant set.

The only mutating command is an argv-based `systemctl --user stop` naming exactly the accepted AllThree fit unit and successful verify-v2 unit. The failed verify-v1 and all other units are outside the command. No model, checkpoint, state, tensor, array, or dataset payload is read or hashed.

The script captures the stop return code/stdout/stderr, both post-command unit states, and post-command parent cgroup/process/event metadata in its JSON output. It reports rather than asserts the stop return code and post-stop states; the root must inspect and independently preserve that result before claiming successful termination.

limitations: This verdict is source-only. It does not establish that the command was run, that either unit stopped, or that any post-stop state or output is valid.

The reviewer did not independently re-read or rehash the acceptance, captured unit.log, remote checker, or provenance payloads; their exact bindings are taken from the supplied root source-binding record and must be enforced by the root's actual-action/result gates.
